title: Salvage icon-only split-button: optimistic-cancel, touch-target, and token inheritance cleanup
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Several regressions surfaced after the recent token migration and split-button feature rollout: (1) icon-only split buttons render a 32px hit target instead of the expected 44px on small density surfaces, (2) optimistic loading states can’t be cancelled reliably on touch devices (users get stuck in spinner state), and (3) theming token inheritance leads to inconsistent tints for icon-only variants in high-contrast modes. This ticket consolidates a design spec and acceptance criteria to unblock engineering and QA work for a patch release.
background_and_rationale: Context: Design tokens were flattened in runtime-1.23 which changed how component variants inherit color and size tokens. Engineering implemented a lightweight split-button variant that attempted to reuse the icon-only surface but missed touch-target and cancellation affordances. Several customer-facing regressions reported by support (Case #10442, #10479) indicate degraded UX in workflows that use compact action rows. Fixing these is high priority due to customer impact on conversion flows.
acceptance_criteria: Icon-only split buttons must meet 44px minimum accessible touch target on mobile/dense surfaces (visual center can remain 32px, but invisible hitbox must expand)
Optimistic loading state supports cancel (tap on icon again) and exposes a clear 'abort' affordance for screen readers (aria-live + role=button state change)
Theming token inheritance: primary/ghost/neutral icon-only variants match Console theme token expectations in light/dark/high-contrast, no hardcoded hex values remain
No visual regressions in the standard button suite (baseline comparison run against snapshot set v2026-02-01)
Automated unit tests cover hitbox math and token cascade fallback for icon-only variant
Telemetry added: event button.cancel_attempt and button.load_stall with sampling 1/100 to detect cancellations and stalls >5s
design_decisions: Prefer invisible hit-target expansion over visual padding to avoid layout shift in dense lists
Expose a cancel affordance via a short-lived overlay on touch (200ms debounce before showing overlay) to avoid accidental cancels
Use token alias --button-surface-interaction-padding to drive hitbox expansion; fallback to --button-touch-padding if undefined
Avoid creating separate icon-only token set; instead fix cascade rules so existing icon tokens inherit correctly from variant tokens
deliverables: Updated Figma components: icon-only-split-button (variants: default/ghost/neutral/primary) - prototype links in design_links
Design spec document with hitbox math, ARIA updates, and theming examples
A/B checklist for roll-back and canary rollout
QA test matrix and automated snapshot run configuration
qa_checklist: Manual: Verify touch target is 44px on iPhone SE, Pixel 4a, and an iPad simulator
Manual: Verify cancel gesture cancels optimistic spinner within 400ms and returns to idle state
Automated: Snapshot diff against baseline v2026-02-01 for 8 permutations (variant x theme)
Accessibility: NVDA/VoiceOver readout includes 'action cancelled' aria-live message
Performance: No increased layout thrashing in compact list view (measure frame drops)
Regression: Run full button test suite and report failures
rollout_plan: Canary on console-2026.03 to 10% of sessions for 48 hours with telemetry gates: if button.load_stall > baseline + 20% or button.cancel_attempt triggered > baseline+10% (indicating unexpected cancels), roll back. Full rollout after 72 hours if no regressions.
notes_for_engineering: Engineering should: (1) consume --button-surface-interaction-padding token and expose a parameter to override per-platform, (2) implement optimistic cancel as idempotent state transition with debounce, (3) add unit tests for token fallback and hitbox math, (4) include telemetry events with sampling to PRs.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Invisible hit-target expansion may overlap adjacent inline controls -> Mitigation: only expand outward away from adjacent interactive surfaces; if overlap unavoidable, fall back to visual padding + motion to indicate expansion
Risk: Theme token fix may change color subtly in edge cases -> Mitigation: create a migration patch that maps old literal hex tokens to new aliases for the next 2 releases and run visual diff checks
